claim1Verbatim:
1. A method of fabricating a multi-state magnetoresistive random access memory (MRAM) device comprising the steps of:
providing a substrate defining a surface;
supporting a base electrode on the surface of the substrate;
and
forming an MRAM cell by
forming a pinned region having a first ferromagnetic layer with a fixed magnetic moment vector fixed in a preferred direction both with and without an applied magnetic field,
forming a material layer in contact with the pinned region, and
forming a free ferromagnetic region adjacent the material layer, wherein the free ferromagnetic region includes a second ferromagnetic layer and has a shape anisotropy that provides a free magnetic moment vector of the second ferromagnetic layer with four stable positions to which the free magnetic moment vector is aligned while writing the MRAM cell, and wherein a first two stable positions of the four stable positions are oriented in opposite directions from each other along a first easy axis, and a second two stable positions of the four stable positions are oriented in opposite directions from each other along a second easy axis, wherein the first easy axis and the second easy axis are at nonzero angles relative to the preferred direction of the fixed magnetic moment vector.

zh.summary: Claim 1 是製作多狀態磁阻隨機存取記憶體（MRAM）裝置的方法項。步驟包括：提供界定表面的基板；在該基板表面上支撐基極電極；以及藉由以下方式形成 MRAM 單元：形成具有第一鐵磁層的釘扎區，該第一鐵磁層具有在有無外加磁場時皆固定於較佳方向的固定磁矩向量；形成與該釘扎區接觸的材料層；以及在該材料層鄰近處形成自由鐵磁區，其中該自由鐵磁區包含第二鐵磁層，並具有形狀各向異性，使該第二鐵磁層的自由磁矩向量具有四個穩定位置，寫入該 MRAM 單元時自由磁矩向量對準這些位置；其中四個穩定位置中的前兩個沿第一易軸彼此相反，後兩個沿第二易軸彼此相反，且第一與第二易軸相對於該固定磁矩向量的較佳方向呈非零角度。本次為有界的文字技術核對，不是法律上的權利範圍判定。
limitations: 前言：一種製作多狀態磁阻隨機存取記憶體（MRAM）裝置的方法，包含下列步驟。
提供界定表面的基板。
在該基板表面上支撐基極電極。
藉由形成釘扎區、材料層與自由鐵磁區來形成 MRAM 單元。
釘扎區具有第一鐵磁層，其固定磁矩向量在有無外加磁場時皆固定於較佳方向。
材料層與該釘扎區接觸。
自由鐵磁區鄰近該材料層（原文為 adjacent the material layer），包含第二鐵磁層，並具有形狀各向異性，使第二鐵磁層的自由磁矩向量具有四個穩定位置，寫入時對準這些位置。
四個穩定位置中的前兩個沿第一易軸彼此相反，後兩個沿第二易軸彼此相反。
第一易軸與第二易軸相對於固定磁矩向量的較佳方向呈非零角度。
zh.dependentClaimBoundary: Claim 9 是另一獨立方法項（在多狀態 MRAM 裝置中儲存多個狀態），不能回寫進 Claim 1。Claims 2–8 與 17 依附 Claim 1：Claim 2 加入靠近基極電極的導線；Claim 3 加入連接基極電極與電氣地的隔離電晶體；Claims 4–5 將材料層限定為氧化鋁或其他合適非鐵磁材料，或銅或其他合適導電材料；Claims 6–7 用極座標方程式或多葉形、或以簇／結晶生長來產生形狀各向異性；Claim 8 加入靠近基極電極的第一導線，以及鄰近自由鐵磁區的第二導線，且四個穩定位置相對這兩條導線呈非零角度；Claim 17 要求四個穩定位置對應四個可在讀取時量測的電阻值。Claims 10–16 依附獨立項 9。這些額外限定與 Claim 9 本身都不可折入 Claim 1。全案印載 Claims 1–17。
zh.specificationBoundary: 題名是多狀態磁阻隨機存取單元與提高儲存密度；摘要描述釘扎鐵磁區、非鐵磁間隔層與具有 N 個（大於二的整數）穩定位置的自由鐵磁區。Claim 1 已是製作方法，且已限定四個穩定位置與兩條易軸的幾何關係，不能改寫成必須採用三層結構、必須使用氧化鋁或銅間隔層、必須以極座標葉形定義形狀，或必須量測四個電阻值（那些是說明書實施例或從屬項）。附圖簡述（第 8 頁第 3 欄）將 FIG. 1 稱為剖面圖、FIG. 2 稱為 FIG. 1 的平面圖（原文 is plan view，缺少冠詞）、FIG. 3 稱為各狀態電阻值的圖；FIGS. 4–5 是寫入脈衝與另一實施例剖面，不能用來把 Claim 1 改寫成必須使用圖中的具體導線佈局或脈衝序列。
unknowns: 未核對現權利人、法律狀態、全球家族或實測性能。
Claim 1 未定義材料層的組成、自由區的具體形狀方程式，也未要求隔離電晶體、第二導線或讀取電阻值。
Claim 1 使用 “adjacent the material layer”，請求項本身未寫 adjacent to。

en.summary: Claim 1 is a method of fabricating a multi-state magnetoresistive random access memory (MRAM) device. The steps are: providing a substrate defining a surface; supporting a base electrode on that surface; and forming an MRAM cell by forming a pinned region having a first ferromagnetic layer with a fixed magnetic moment vector fixed in a preferred direction both with and without an applied magnetic field, forming a material layer in contact with the pinned region, and forming a free ferromagnetic region adjacent the material layer, wherein that free region includes a second ferromagnetic layer and has a shape anisotropy that provides the second layer’s free magnetic moment vector with four stable positions to which the vector is aligned while writing the cell, and wherein a first two of those positions are oriented in opposite directions along a first easy axis, a second two are oriented in opposite directions along a second easy axis, and the two easy axes are at nonzero angles relative to the preferred direction of the fixed magnetic moment vector. This is a bounded technical text check, not a legal determination of claim scope.
limitations: Preamble: a method of fabricating a multi-state magnetoresistive random access memory (MRAM) device comprising the steps of.
Providing a substrate defining a surface.
Supporting a base electrode on the surface of the substrate.
Forming an MRAM cell by forming a pinned region, a material layer, and a free ferromagnetic region.
The pinned region has a first ferromagnetic layer with a fixed magnetic moment vector fixed in a preferred direction both with and without an applied magnetic field.
The material layer is in contact with the pinned region.

The free ferromagnetic region is adjacent the material layer (so worded), includes a second ferromagnetic layer, and has a shape anisotropy that provides a free magnetic moment vector of the second ferromagnetic layer with four stable positions to which the vector is aligned while writing the MRAM cell.

A first two of the four stable positions are oriented in opposite directions from each other along a first easy axis, and a second two are oriented in opposite directions from each other along a second easy axis.
The first easy axis and the second easy axis are at nonzero angles relative to the preferred direction of the fixed magnetic moment vector.
en.dependentClaimBoundary: Claim 9 is a separate independent method (a method of storing multiple states in a multi-state MRAM device) and is not folded into Claim 1. Claims 2–8 and 17 depend from claim 1: claim 2 adds a conductive line proximate to the base electrode; claim 3 adds connecting an isolation transistor to the base electrode and an electrical ground; claims 4–5 require that the material layer include aluminum oxide or another suitable non-ferromagnetic material, or copper or another suitable conductive material; claims 6–7 define the shape anisotropy by a polar equation that yields a multi-lobe shape, or by growing the free region with clusters or crystallites; claim 8 adds a conductive line proximate to the base electrode and a second conductive line adjacent to the free ferromagnetic region, with the four stable positions at nonzero angles relative to those lines; claim 17 requires that each of the four stable positions correspond to one of four resistance values that may be measured while reading the cell. Claims 10–16 depend from independent claim 9. Those added limitations, and claim 9 itself, are not folded into Claim 1. Claims 1–17 are the claims printed in the grant.
en.specificationBoundary: The title concerns a multi-state magnetoresistance random access cell with improved memory storage density; the abstract describes a pinned ferromagnetic region, a non-ferromagnetic spacer, and a free ferromagnetic region with N stable positions, N being a whole number greater than two. Claim 1 is already a fabrication method, and it already requires four stable positions and the two-easy-axis geometry; it cannot be rewritten as requiring a tri-layer stack, an aluminum-oxide or copper spacer, a polar-equation lobe shape, or measurement of four resistance values (those are embodiments or dependent claims). The brief description of the drawings (page 8, column 3) calls FIG. 1 a sectional view, FIG. 2 a plan view of the device of FIG. 1 (printed “is plan view,” without an article), and FIG. 3 a graph of resistance values in the various states. FIGS. 4–5 are write-pulse graphs and a sectional view of another embodiment, and cannot be used to rewrite Claim 1 as requiring the illustrated line layout or pulse sequence.
unknowns: Current title holder, legal status, global family, and measured performance were not verified.

Claim 1 does not define the composition of the material layer, a specific shape equation for the free region, or any requirement for an isolation transistor, a second conductive line, or read-time resistance values.
Claim 1 uses the phrase “adjacent the material layer”; the claim itself does not say “adjacent to.”

note.zh: FIG. 1 在第 5 頁（Sheet 1 of 2），為多層剖面，標示單元 5、基極電極 14、導線 12、隔離電晶體 10／13 與多層鐵磁／非鐵磁堆疊。附圖簡述（第 8 頁第 3 欄）稱為多狀態磁阻隨機存取記憶體裝置的剖面圖。這是結構實施例；Claim 1 雖要求基極電極、釘扎區、材料層與自由鐵磁區，但並未限定必須採用圖中的具體層數、導線或隔離電晶體（隔離電晶體是 Claim 3）。
note.en: FIG. 1 is on PDF page 5 (Sheet 1 of 2). It is a sectional stack showing cell 5, base electrode 14, conductive line 12, isolation transistor 10/13, and a multilayer ferromagnetic/non-ferromagnetic stack. The brief description (page 8, column 3) calls it a sectional view of a multi-state magnetoresistive random access memory device. That is a structural embodiment. Claim 1 does require a base electrode, a pinned region, a material layer, and a free ferromagnetic region, but it does not require the illustrated layer count, conductive line, or isolation transistor (the isolation transistor is claim 3).

note.zh: FIG. 2 同在第 5 頁，為平面圖，顯示四個穩定位置 50、52、54、56 與易軸、以及導線 12 與 36。附圖簡述稱為 FIG. 1 所示裝置的平面圖（原文 is plan view）。圖中的具體軸向與導線佈局是實施例；Claim 1 已要求四個穩定位置與兩條互成非零角的易軸，但不能把圖中的 90° 座標或雙導線寫入 Claim 1。
note.en: FIG. 2 is also on PDF page 5. It is a plan view showing four stable positions 50, 52, 54, and 56, the easy axes, and conductive lines 12 and 36. The brief description calls it a plan view of the device illustrated in FIG. 1 (printed “is plan view”). The particular axes and line layout are an embodiment. Claim 1 already requires four stable positions and two easy axes at nonzero angles, but the illustrated 90° coordinate frame and dual conductive lines are not to be folded into Claim 1.

note.zh: FIG. 3 在第 6 頁（Sheet 2 of 2），為電阻值圖，標示 R00、R01、R10、R11 與磁矩向量。附圖簡述稱為各狀態電阻值的圖。四個電阻值是揭露與從屬項 17 的內容，不是 Claim 1 的必要限制；Claim 1 講的是寫入時對準的四個穩定位置，並未要求讀取電阻。
note.en: FIG. 3 is on PDF page 6 (Sheet 2 of 2). It is a resistance graph labeled R00, R01, R10, and R11, with moment vectors. The brief description calls it a graph illustrating the resistance values of a multi-state magnetoresistive random access memory device in the various states. The four resistance values are disclosure, and appear in dependent claim 17; they are not limitations of Claim 1, which recites four stable positions to which the free moment is aligned while writing and does not require a read of resistance.

zh.summary: Claim 1 是電路項。該電路包含：第一組件，用以接收與第一命令相關的第一信號以及與第二命令相關的第二信號，第一信號使該電路啟動與第一命令相關的第一系列事件，第二信號「indicating to cause」該電路啟動與第二命令相關的第二系列事件（原文如此，依印刷登錄）；以及重疊組件，配置為延遲第一系列事件的 initialization，直到與第二命令相關的第二系列事件完成。本次為有界的文字技術核對，不是法律上的權利範圍判定。
limitations: 前言：一種電路。
第一組件用以接收與第一命令相關的第一信號，以及與第二命令相關的第二信號。
第一信號使該電路啟動與第一命令相關的第一系列事件。
第二信號 indicating to cause 該電路啟動與第二命令相關的第二系列事件（原文）。
重疊組件配置為延遲第一系列事件的 initialization，直到與第二命令相關的第二系列事件完成。
zh.dependentClaimBoundary: Claims 7 與 12 是另外的獨立項，不能回寫進 Claim 1。Claim 7 是包含預充電時序單元與啟動時序單元的電路，並要求兩系列事件在一段期間屆滿前完成，該期間是外部來源在提供預充電命令後等待的時脈週期數，加上在提供啟動命令後等待的時脈週期數。Claim 12 是記憶裝置，其重疊電路防止與第二命令相關的操作開始，直到從已接收第一命令的時序單元收到完成信號——也就是延遲第二系列直到第一系列完成，與 Claim 1 的印刷文字不同。Claims 2–6 依附 Claim 1：Claim 2 將第一組件限定為命令解譯器；Claim 3 加入用以啟動第二系列個別事件的時序單元；Claim 4 再加入用以啟動第一系列個別事件的第二時序單元；Claims 5–6 將第一命令限定為啟動（activate）命令，將第二命令限定為預充電命令。Claims 8–11 依附 7；Claims 13–20 依附 12。這些額外限定與另兩個獨立項都不可折入 Claim 1。全案印載 Claims 1–20。
zh.specificationBoundary: 題名與摘要討論具有時序重疊模式的記憶裝置。摘要寫的是記憶裝置延遲第二系列事件的開始，直到第一系列事件完成；說明書與獨立項 12 也是這個方向。Claim 1 印刷文字則是延遲第一系列的 initialization，直到第二系列完成，並且只是「電路」，未在前言寫成記憶裝置，也未寫預充電或啟動。不能用摘要、tRP／tRCD 時序或 FIG. 3 的命令順序，把 Claim 1 改寫成必須延遲第二系列，或必須是預充電／啟動記憶操作。附圖簡述（第 8 頁第 1 欄）將 FIGS. 1–2 稱為在執行操作時接收命令的例示系統組件，將 FIG. 3 稱為與 FIGS. 1 與 2 相關的時序圖。命令解譯器、預充電／啟動時序單元與 AND 閘重疊電路是實施例或從屬項／其他獨立項。本項是從本公報官方 PDF 讀出，並非自同族 US9552849B2 抄錄。
unknowns: 未核對現權利人、法律狀態、全球家族或實測性能。
Claim 1 未定義第一／第二命令的種類、第一組件或重疊組件的電路結構，也未使用 initialization 與 initiate 是否同義。
Claim 1 的 “indicating to cause” 依印刷登錄；請求項本身未另作解釋。

en.summary: Claim 1 is a circuit. It comprises a first component to receive a first signal associated with a first command and a second signal associated with a second command, the first signal to cause the circuit to initiate a first series of events associated with the first command and the second signal indicating to cause the circuit to initiate a second series of events associated with the second command (so worded, recorded as printed); and an overlap component configured to delay the initialization of the first series of events until the second series of events associated with the second command are complete. This is a bounded technical text check, not a legal determination of claim scope.
limitations: Preamble: a circuit.
A first component to receive a first signal associated with a first command and a second signal associated with a second command.
The first signal is to cause the circuit to initiate a first series of events associated with the first command.
The second signal is “indicating to cause” the circuit to initiate a second series of events associated with the second command (as printed).
An overlap component configured to delay the initialization of the first series of events until the second series of events associated with the second command are complete.
en.dependentClaimBoundary: Claims 7 and 12 are separate independent claims and are not folded into Claim 1. Claim 7 is a circuit with a precharge timing unit and an activate timing unit, and it requires that both series of events complete before a period expires, that period being a number of clock cycles an external source waits after providing the precharge command plus a number of clock cycles it waits after providing the activate command. Claim 12 is a memory device whose overlap circuit prevents initiation of operations associated with the second command until a completion signal is received from the timing unit that received the first command—that is, it delays the second series until the first completes, which is not the wording printed in Claim 1. Claims 2–6 depend from claim 1: claim 2 requires that the first component is a command interpreter; claim 3 adds a timing unit to initiate individual events of the second series; claim 4, through 3, adds a second timing unit to initiate individual events of the first series; claims 5–6 require that the first command is an activate command and that the second command is a precharge command. Claims 8–11 depend from 7; claims 13–20 depend from 12. Those added limitations, and the other two independent claims, are not folded into Claim 1. Claims 1–20 are the claims printed in the grant.
en.specificationBoundary: The title and abstract concern a memory device with a timing overlap mode. The abstract says the memory device delays the start of the second series of events until the first series completes; the detailed description and independent claim 12 are in that direction as well. Claim 1 as printed instead delays initialization of the first series until the second series is complete, and it is only “a circuit,” not a memory device in the preamble, and it does not recite precharge or activate. The abstract, the tRP/tRCD timing discussion, and the command order in FIG. 3 cannot be used to rewrite Claim 1 as requiring delay of the second series, or as a precharge/activate memory operation. The brief description of the drawings (page 8, column 1) calls FIGS. 1–2 select components of example systems including a memory device to receive a command while executing an operation, and FIG. 3 a timing diagram associated with the memory devices of FIGS. 1 and 2. A command interpreter, precharge and activate timing units, and an AND-gate overlap circuit are embodiments or belong to dependent claims or to the other independent claims. The text was read from this official PDF and was not copied from related-family US9552849B2.
unknowns: Current title holder, legal status, global family, and measured performance were not verified.

en.summary: Claim 1 is a method of reading a data state stored in a magnetic tunnel junction cell. The steps are: applying an oscillating signal to the cell to read the data state stored therein, wherein applying the oscillating signal includes applying an oscillating voltage across the cell that causes an oscillating resistance of the cell, wherein that oscillating resistance has a same frequency of oscillation as the oscillating voltage (so worded); measuring a time-independent DC signal across the cell while applying the oscillating signal, the time-independent DC signal being generated by the cell in response to applying the oscillating signal and being a product of the oscillating resistance and the oscillating voltage; and determining the stored data state by comparing the time-independent DC signal to a reference signal. This is a bounded technical text check, not a legal determination of claim scope.
limitations: Preamble: a method of reading a data state stored in a magnetic tunnel junction cell.
Applying an oscillating signal to the magnetic tunnel junction cell to read the data state stored therein.
Applying the oscillating signal includes applying an oscillating voltage across the cell that causes an oscillating resistance of the cell.
The oscillating resistance of the cell has a same frequency of oscillation as the oscillating voltage (as printed).
Measuring a time-independent DC signal across the cell while applying the oscillating signal.
The time-independent DC signal is generated by the cell in response to applying the oscillating signal, and is a product of the oscillating resistance and the oscillating voltage.
Determining the data state stored in the cell by comparing the time-independent DC signal to a reference signal.
en.dependentClaimBoundary: Claims 8 and 14 are separate independent apparatus claims and are not folded into Claim 1. Claim 8 is a random access memory comprising a programmable memory bit having first and second resistance states, a sensing unit configured to apply an oscillating signal, and read logic selectively coupled to read the bit. Claim 14 is a magnetoresistive random access memory comprising an array of MTJ cells, a sensing unit electrically coupled to the array, and read logic. Claims 2–7 depend from claim 1: claim 2 requires applying the oscillating signal through the MTJ cell; claim 3 adds causing a frequency of the oscillating signal to match a resonance frequency of the cell in a high state or a low state; claim 4 adds applying an additional bias signal to increase a resistance non-linearity; claim 5 requires applying the oscillating signal through a conductive line located near the cell; claim 6, through 2, requires that the oscillating signal comprise a current having an amplitude substantially lower than an average switching current of the cell; claim 7, through 5, requires applying a magnetic field having an amplitude substantially lower than an average switching field of a plurality of cells. Claims 9–13 depend from 8; claims 15–20 depend from 14. Those added limitations, and the other two independent claims, are not folded into Claim 1. Claims 1–20 are the claims printed in the grant.
en.specificationBoundary: The title is a random access memory architecture for reading bit states; the abstract and brief summary call the measured signal a rectified signal. Claim 1 is already a method of reading a data state stored in an MTJ cell, and it uses the term “time-independent DC signal”; it cannot be rewritten as an architecture, as a method that must measure a “rectified” signal, or as a method that must use a microwave current, a 100 ns voltage pulse, or an external holding field (those are conditions in the brief description of FIGS. 2–3). The brief description of the drawings (page 5, column 2) calls FIG. 1 a graph of typical normalized resistance of a magnetic bit as a function of applied magnetic field, FIG. 2 a graph of normalized rectified voltage of a magnetic bit subjected to a microwave current as a function of applied magnetic field, and FIG. 3 a graph of normalized resistance as a function of an applied voltage pulse of 100 ns while a strong external magnetic field maintained the bit in a given state. FIGS. 4–6 are readout-circuit and flowchart embodiments, and the flowchart uses “rectified signal” language; they cannot be used to rewrite Claim 1.

This is a bounded technical text check, not a legal determination of claim scope.

Claim 14 is a separate method of providing a boosted voltage at a node on a device, in which the generator is deactivated in response to the signal transition and state information is stored. Claims 2–7 depend from claim 1: claims 2–3 add deactivating the voltage generator before driving the signal line or before performing the operation; claim 4 requires that driving the signal line further comprises driving a word line in a magnetic memory device; claims 5–7 add storing state information corresponding to deactivation, stopping provision of a clock and later providing the clock based on a stored clock state, or a charge pump with precharging of internal nodes. Claims 9–13 depend from 8; claims 15–20 depend from 14. Those added limitations, and the other two independent claims, are not folded into Claim 1. Claims 1–20 are the claims printed in the grant.
en.specificationBoundary: The title and abstract concern a boosted supply voltage generator for a memory device; the brief description of the drawings (page 5, column 2) still describes FIGS. 1–4 in word-line and memory-device terms. 一個電路，用以接收使該電路執行第一操作的第一命令，以及使該電路執行第二操作的第二命令。

en.summary: Claim 1 is a memory device. It comprises a circuit to receive a first command to cause the circuit to perform a first operation and a second command to cause the circuit to perform a second operation; wherein the first operation and the second operation are completed by the circuit prior to an expiration of a period of time, the period of time representing a number of clock cycles that an external source waits after providing the first command plus a number of clock cycles the external source waits after providing the second command (the second clause is printed without “that” before “the external source,” recorded as printed). This is a bounded technical text check, not a legal determination of claim scope. The text was read from this official PDF and was not copied from parent US9230633B2.
limitations: Preamble: a memory device.
A circuit to receive a first command to cause the circuit to perform a first operation and a second command to cause the circuit to perform a second operation.
The first operation and the second operation are completed by the circuit prior to an expiration of a period of time.

The period of time represents a number of clock cycles that an external source waits after providing the first command plus a number of clock cycles the external source waits after providing the second command (as printed).
en.dependentClaimBoundary: Claims 8 and 15 are separate independent claims and are not folded into Claim 1. Claim 8 is a system comprising a circuit to generate first and second commands, and a memory device that, at least in part in response to receiving the first command, initiates a first operation associated with the first command and temporarily prevents an initiation of a second operation associated with the second command. Claim 15 is a method comprising receiving, at a circuit, a command from an external source associated with accessing data stored in a memory device; generating, by the circuit, a control signal to at least in part initiate a series of events related to the command; receiving an additional command and a signal indicating a completion of the series of events; and generating an additional control signal to at least in part initiate an additional series of events. Claims 2–7 depend from claim 1: claim 2 requires a precharge timing circuit to perform the first operation, an activate timing circuit to perform the second operation, and an overlap circuit to delay an initiation of the second operation until a completion of the first operation; claim 3, through 2, adds loading a new page of data into a cache; claim 4 requires that the two wait periods are a row-precharge-time and a row-address-to-column-address delay; claim 5 adds a read sample operation, applying a reset voltage to a bit line or a source line, and a read evaluate operation; claim 6 adds an overlap circuit and requires that the operations relate to writing between a cache and a memory bank; claim 7 requires that the first operation relate to writing cache content into a memory bank, and that the device is a magnetic random access memory that requires more clock cycles to perform the first operation than the external source waits after providing the first command. Claims 9–14 depend from 8; claims 16–20 depend from 15. Those added limitations, and the other two independent claims, are not folded into Claim 1. Claims 1–20 are the claims printed in the grant.
en.specificationBoundary: The title adds a precharge timing circuit; the abstract says the memory device delays the start of the second series of events until the first series completes. Claim 1 of parent US9230633B2 is a circuit with a first component and an overlap component, and as printed it delays initialization of the first series until the second series is complete. Claim 1 here is already a memory device, and it only requires that a circuit complete first and second operations before a combined external-source wait period expires; the abstract, tRP/tRCD, the precharge-then-activate order in FIG. 3, and the parent claim cannot be used to rewrite it as requiring an overlap circuit, precharge and activate operations, or delay of the second operation until the first completes (those are dependent claims 2–5 or disclosure). The brief description of the drawings (page 8, column 1) calls FIGS. 1–2 select components of example systems including a memory device to receive a command while executing an operation, and FIG. 3 a timing diagram associated with the memory devices of FIGS. 1 and 2.
unknowns: Current title holder, legal status, global family, and measured performance were not verified.

This is a bounded technical text check, not a legal determination of claim scope.
limitations: Preamble: a memory device.

Claims 2–7 and 20 depend from claim 1: claim 2 requires that the sample signal and the regulated write signal be a voltage or a current; claims 3–4 require that identifying the resistive value include measuring a current or a voltage differential and translating it into the resistive value; claim 5 requires a drive component and a sample component; claim 6 requires that the two access points be associated with the bit cell so as to apply the signals to that cell and prevent application to other bit cells; claim 7 requires that the access points also be associated with at least a second bit cell; claim 20 requires that the write circuitry identify the resistive value prior to causing the state of the bit cell to switch. en.summary: Claim 1 is a method of forming a nanotube switching element. The method comprises forming a first structure having at least one output electrode; forming a nanotube layer and lithographically defining a shape of a conductive article by lithographically patterning the layer and removing portions of the layer to form a conductive article having at least one nanotube; wherein the at least one nanotube is substantially parallel to a substrate having the nanotube switching element (after this wherein clause the official page prints a gap and no semicolon, then continues with the next step; that typography is recorded as printed and is not repaired); forming a second structure having at least one output electrode and positioning said second structure in relation to the first structure and the conductive article such that the output electrode of the first structure is opposite the output electrode of the second structure and such that a portion of the conductive article is positioned therebetween; providing at least one signal electrode in electrical communication with the conductive article having at least one nanotube; and providing at least one control electrode in relation to the conductive article such that the control electrode may control the conductive article to form a channel between the signal electrode and at least one of the output electrodes. This is a bounded textual technical review, not a legal determination of claim scope.
limitations: The method is a method of forming a nanotube switching element.
A first structure having at least one output electrode is formed.

A nanotube layer is formed, and a shape of a conductive article is lithographically defined by lithographically patterning the layer and removing portions of the layer to form a conductive article having at least one nanotube.

The at least one nanotube is substantially parallel to a substrate having the nanotube switching element. After this wherein clause the official page prints a gap and no semicolon; that typography is recorded as printed.

A second structure having at least one output electrode is formed, and said second structure is positioned in relation to the first structure and the conductive article such that the output electrode of the first structure is opposite the output electrode of the second structure and such that a portion of the conductive article is positioned therebetween.
At least one signal electrode is provided in electrical communication with the conductive article having at least one nanotube.

At least one control electrode is provided in relation to the conductive article such that the control electrode may control the conductive article to form a channel between the signal electrode and at least one of the output electrodes.
en.dependentClaimBoundary: The independents are claim 1 (method) and claim 14 (a separate method of forming a nanotube switching element, printed at PDF page 36, column 18). Claims 2–13 depend, directly or indirectly, from claim 1. Claim 2 further provides a second control electrode, prints “unform a channel,” and places the control electrode and the second control electrode on opposite sides of the conductive article. Claim 3, depending from claim 2, adds a switching-region cavity in which the conductive article is at least partially suspended and electrostatically deflectable in response to electrical activation of at least one of the control electrode and the second control electrode. Claim 4, depending from claim 1, gives each of the first and second structures a respective second output electrode, with those second output electrodes opposite each other and the conductive article positioned therebetween. Claim 5 ties together the output electrodes of the first and second structures. Claim 6, depending from claim 4, ties together the second output electrodes. Claim 7, depending from claim 2, gives each control electrode an insulator layer on a surface facing the conductive article. Claims 8–13 add insulator layers on output electrodes, sub-lithographic defining areas, spaced relations of different magnitudes, and output / second-output electrodes positioned symmetrically about a control electrode. Claim 14 is an independent method whose first structure already has a first output electrode and a first control electrode, whose conductive-article forming step is not Claim 1’s “forming a nanotube layer and lithographically patterning / removing” sequence, and which positions the second structure so as to clamp the conductive article and suspend a central portion, with the first output opposite the second output and the first control opposite the second control. The second control electrode, cavity / deflection, second output electrodes, tying, insulator layers, clamp-and-suspend arrangement, and claim 14’s architecture are not folded into Claim 1. The grant prints 14 claims, matching the page-2 footer.

The detailed description describes FIG. 1A as a preferred nanotube switching element 100, with a release electrode 112, output electrodes 113a,b, an input electrode 111, output channels 113c,d and signal electrodes 114a,b over an insulating layer 117, and a nanotube channel 115 positioned and held by upper and lower portions. en.summary: Claim 1 is a non-volatile field effect device. The device comprises a source, drain and gate with a field-modulatable channel between the source and drain, each of the source, drain, and gate having a corresponding terminal; an electromechanically-deflectable, nanotube switching element electrically positioned between one of the source, drain and gate and its corresponding terminal, the others of said source, drain and gate being directly connected to their corresponding terminals; wherein the nanotube switching element is electromechanically-deflectable in response to electrical stimulation at two control terminals to create one of a non-volatile open and non-volatile closed electrical communication state between the one of the source, drain and gate and its corresponding terminal. The printed hyphenation of “field-modulatable” and “electromechanically-deflectable,” and the phrase “one of a non-volatile open and non-volatile closed,” are recorded as printed. This is a bounded textual technical review, not a legal determination of claim scope.
limitations: The claimed object is a non-volatile field effect device.

An electromechanically-deflectable, nanotube switching element is electrically positioned between one of the source, drain and gate and its corresponding terminal.
The others of said source, drain and gate are directly connected to their corresponding terminals.

The nanotube switching element is electromechanically-deflectable in response to electrical stimulation at two control terminals to create one of a non-volatile open and non-volatile closed electrical communication state between the one of the source, drain and gate and its corresponding terminal.
en.dependentClaimBoundary: Claim 1 is the only independent claim. Claims 2–18 all depend, directly or indirectly, from claim 1, and all 18 printed claims are device claims. The grant prints 18 claims, matching the page-2 footer. The printed title also refers to methods of forming the devices, but no method claim is printed among claims 1–18. Claim 2 has the nanotube switching element include an article formed of nanotube fabric; claim 3, depending from claim 2, limits that fabric to a porous nanotube fabric; claim 6, depending from claim 2, limits the nanotubes to single-walled carbon nanotubes. Claim 4 gives one of the two control terminals a dielectric surface for contact with the nanotube switching element when creating a non-volatile open state. Claim 5 adds voltage ranges for the source, drain and gate and for the two control terminals. Claim 7 has modulation of the channel region include inverting the conductivity type of the channel region. Claim 8, though depending from claim 1, prints “the fabric,” a term first introduced in claim 2. Claim 9 adds an article made from nanofabric positioned between the two control terminals; claims 10–12 then add a release electrode and a set electrode. Claim 13 limits the device to only four terminals to control its operation. Claim 14 adds that, in a closed state, channel conductivity and device operation are responsive to electrical stimulus at the terminals corresponding to the source, gate and drain. Claim 15 adds on and off modes and prints “the device the source, drain, and gate may be used to module the channel.” Claim 16 limits the device to a memory cell and prints “non-volatily stored.” Claims 17–18, depending from claim 15, add that in the on mode the source signal is a digital or analog inversion of the gate signal. Fabric / porous / single-wall, a dielectric surface, the voltage ranges, conductivity-type inversion, release / set electrodes, a four-terminal-only limit, a memory cell, and the on/off modes are not folded into Claim 1.

en.summary: Claim 1 is a switching element. The element comprises an input node; an output node; a nanotube channel element having at least one electrically conductive nanotube; a control electrode disposed in relation to the nanotube channel element to form an electrically conductive channel between said input node and said output node, wherein said channel at least includes said nanotube channel element; and wherein said output node is constructed and arranged so that channel formation is substantially unaffected by the electrical state of the output node. The preamble prints “A switching element, comprising” with no colon after “comprising”; that typography is recorded as printed and is not repaired. This is a bounded textual technical review, not a legal determination of claim scope.
limitations: The claimed object is a switching element. The preamble has no colon after “comprising”; that typography is recorded as printed.
The element has an input node and an output node.
The element has a nanotube channel element having at least one electrically conductive nanotube.

A control electrode is disposed in relation to the nanotube channel element to form an electrically conductive channel between said input node and said output node, and said channel at least includes said nanotube channel element.
Said output node is constructed and arranged so that channel formation is substantially unaffected by the electrical state of the output node.
en.dependentClaimBoundary: Claim 1 is the only independent claim. Claims 2–18 all depend, directly or indirectly, from claim 1, and all 18 printed claims are switching-element device claims. The grant prints 18 claims, matching the front-page footer. Claim 2 first adds that the control electrode is arranged to form said conductive channel by causing electromechanical deflection of said nanotube channel element; claim 3, depending from claim 2, has that deflection cause the nanotube channel element to physically contact the output terminal. Claim 4, depending from claim 1, has the output node include an isolation structure so that channel formation is substantially invariant from the state of the output node. Claims 5–7, depending from claim 4/5, add electrostatic deflection, an isolation structure that causes an electrostatic field to insulate the physical position from disturbance by the state of the output node, and electrodes on opposite sides that produce substantially equal but opposite electrostatic forces or that are in low-resistance electrical communication with one another. Claims 8–10 add electrical communication with the input node, a spaced and crossed relation relative to the control electrode, and different spaced distances. Claim 11 adds a lithographically-defined shape; claims 12–14 add construction from nanofabric, highly porous nanofabric, or a substantial monolayer of nanotubes. Claim 15 covers the control electrode with an insulator. Claim 16 adds at least two positional states, one of which is a floating state not in electrical communication with said output node. Claim 17 has the output node include two pairs of output electrodes. Claim 18 further includes a second control electrode, with the control electrode and the second control electrode positioned on different sides of the output node. Electromechanical deflection, physical contact, an isolation structure, nanofabric / a monolayer, an insulator covering, a floating state, two pairs of output electrodes, and a second control electrode are not folded into Claim 1.

en.summary: Claim 1 is a master-slave flip-flop circuit. The circuit comprises a data input; a first clock input and a second clock input for providing non-overlapping first and second clock signals; a first input buffer coupled to the data input and the first clock input for gating the data input under the control of the first clock input; a master storage element coupled to the input buffer for storing a first data value representative of the data input, wherein the master storage element is constructed of at least one nanotube switching element; a second input buffer coupled to the master storage element and the second clock input for gating the first data value under the control of the second clock input; a slave storage element coupled to the second input buffer for storing a second data value representative of the first data value, wherein the slave storage element is constructed of at least one nanotube switching element; and a data output coupled to the slave storage element. After introducing “a first input buffer,” the official text prints “coupled to the input buffer,” not “the first input buffer”; that wording is recorded as printed. The conjunction “and” is printed on its own line before the data-output element. This is a bounded textual technical review, not a legal determination of claim scope.
limitations: The claimed object is a master-slave flip-flop circuit.
The circuit has a data input.
The circuit has a first clock input and a second clock input for providing non-overlapping first and second clock signals.
A first input buffer is coupled to the data input and the first clock input for gating the data input under the control of the first clock input.

A master storage element is coupled to the input buffer (printed that way after “a first input buffer”) for storing a first data value representative of the data input, and is constructed of at least one nanotube switching element.
A second input buffer is coupled to the master storage element and the second clock input for gating the first data value under the control of the second clock input.
A slave storage element is coupled to the second input buffer for storing a second data value representative of the first data value, and is constructed of at least one nanotube switching element.
A data output is coupled to the slave storage element.
en.dependentClaimBoundary: Claim 1 is the only independent claim. Claims 2–12 all depend, directly or indirectly, from claim 1, and all 12 printed claims are circuit claims. The grant prints 12 claims, matching the front-page footer. Claim 2 makes the data input, the first data value, the second data value and the data output differential. Claim 3 makes the master and slave storage elements non-volatile; claim 4 has them constructed using non-volatile four-terminal nanotube switching elements. Claim 5 makes the master and slave storage elements volatile; claim 6, depending from claim 5, has them constructed using volatile three-terminal nanotube switching elements. Claim 7 has at least one of the master or slave storage element constructed using a first nanotube switching element-based inverter and a second nanotube switching element-based inverter; claim 8, depending from claim 7, cross-couples those inverters. Claim 9 has at least one of the first or second input buffer include a nanotube switching element; claims 10–11, depending from claim 9, further limit that buffer to a nanotube switch-based tri-stating inverter or a single nanotube switching element. Claim 12 further comprises an output driver circuit coupled between the slave storage element and the output, constructed using nanotube switching elements. Differential signaling, non-volatile / volatile character, four-terminal / three-terminal construction, inverters / cross-coupling, buffers themselves made of nanotube switches, and an output driver circuit are not folded into Claim 1.
en.specificationBoundary: The brief description of the drawings (PDF page 27, column 5) calls FIG. 1 a schematic illustration of a prior-art circuit including a master-slave storage device; FIG. 2 a schematic illustration of a prior-art master-slave storage device; and FIGS. 3A–D illustrations of an exemplary nanotube switching element used in certain embodiments of the invention. The detailed description (starting at page 27, column 6) describes FIG. 1 as a prior-art digital logic circuit 10 with an input master-slave latch 20, combinational logic 30, and an output master-slave latch 40, and FIG. 2 as a prior-art CMOS master-slave latch 50. FIGS. 3A–D are cross-section, plan, and open/closed views of the nanotube switching element itself, not of the Claim 1 master-slave flip-flop. A four-terminal construction is closer to claim 4 and cannot be used to rewrite Claim 1.

en.summary: Claim 1 is a method of making an article. The method comprises providing a substrate; applying preformed nanotubes to a surface of the substrate to create a non-woven fabric of carbon nanotubes; and selectively removing portions of the non-woven fabric by etching the fabric according to a defined pattern to create the article. Claim 1 prints “preformed nanotubes,” without a hyphen, even though the printed title uses PRE-FORMED and several later dependent claims print “pre-formed”; that wording is recorded as printed. This is a bounded textual technical review, not a legal determination of claim scope.
limitations: The claimed object is a method of making an article.
A substrate is provided.
Preformed nanotubes are applied to a surface of the substrate to create a non-woven fabric of carbon nanotubes.
Portions of the non-woven fabric are selectively removed by etching the fabric according to a defined pattern to create the article.
en.dependentClaimBoundary: Claim 1 is the only independent claim. Claims 2–41 all depend, directly or indirectly, from claim 1, and all 41 printed claims are method claims. The grant prints 41 claims, matching the front-page footer. Claim 2 further includes functionalizing the surface to promote adhesion of the preformed nanotubes; claims 3–4, depending from claim 2, further limit that step to derivitizing or oxidizing the surface. Claims 5–12 concern silane, APTS solutions, hexane immersion, or a silane monolayer. Claims 13 and 26–31 limit the applying step to spinning or multiple spin-coating operations. Claims 14–17 limit the preformed nanotubes to laser-ablated, high-pressure carbon monoxide decomposition, single-walled, or multi-walled nanotubes. Claims 18–25 concern solvent concentration, dispersion, and sonication. Claim 32 requires the applying step to yield a non-woven fabric characterized by a resistance of about 1–1000 kΩ/□. Claim 33 requires subsequent annealing. Claims 34–38 concern controlling or selectively removing metallic and semiconducting nanotubes. Claims 39–40 require the non-woven fabric to cover the substrate and to be of substantially uniform density, or to be about 2 nm or less in thickness. en.summary: Claim 1 is a resistive-element device. The element comprises a patterned region of nanofabric with a predefined area and a pre-selected sheet resistance, the nanofabric having a pre-selected temperature coefficient of resistance (TCR); and first and second electrical contacts contacting the patterned region of nanofabric and in spaced relation to each other. A first wherein clause states that a total resistance of the resistive element between the first and second electrical contacts is determined by the predefined area of the patterned region of nanofabric, the pre-selected sheet resistance of the patterned region of nanofabric between the first and second electrical contacts, and the pre-selected TCR of the nanofabric, and the spaced relation of the first and second electrical contacts. That list prints two coordinating “and”s, which are recorded as printed. A further “and” is printed on its own line before a second wherein clause, which states that the total resistance is tunable to a pre-selected total resistance. This is a bounded textual technical review, not a legal determination of claim scope.
limitations: The claimed object is a resistive element.
The element has a patterned region of nanofabric with a predefined area and a pre-selected sheet resistance, the nanofabric having a pre-selected temperature coefficient of resistance (TCR).
First and second electrical contacts contact the patterned region of nanofabric and are in spaced relation to each other.

A total resistance of the resistive element between the first and second electrical contacts is determined by the predefined area of the patterned region of nanofabric, the pre-selected sheet resistance of that patterned region between the contacts, the pre-selected TCR of the nanofabric, and the spaced relation of the contacts (the first wherein list prints two coordinating “and”s, recorded as printed).
The total resistance is tunable to a pre-selected total resistance.
en.dependentClaimBoundary: Claim 1 is an independent device claim, but it is not the only independent claim. Claim 32, beginning at PDF page 18, columns 11–12, is a separate independent method of making a resistive element. Claims 2–31 all depend, directly or indirectly, from claim 1; claims 33–63 all depend, directly or indirectly, from claim 32. The grant prints 63 claims, matching the front-page footer. Limits depending from claim 1 include: claim 2’s numerical TCR range (about 25 ppm/°C to -25 ppm/°C); claims 3–6 selecting TCR by a ratio of metallic and semiconducting nanotubes; claim 7’s current-carrying capacity (about 1 milliamp per micron of width); claims 8, 11 and 30–31 pre-selecting sheet resistance or TCR by porosity or by minimizing defects; claim 9 tuning total resistance by cutting the nanofabric; claim 10’s sheet-resistance range (1 k-Ohm/square to 1 M-Ohm/square); claims 12–21 on contact termination, metal layers, a passivation layer, a packaged resistor or an integrated circuit, and wire bonding or conductive bumps; claims 22–27 on single-walled nanotubes, a conformal monolayer, metallic or semiconducting nanotubes, or series or parallel combinations; claim 28 stable operation up to at least about 1000 degrees Celsius; and claim 29 laser-scribability. Those limits, and the entire independent method of claim 32, are not folded into Claim 1.
en.specificationBoundary: The brief description of the drawings (PDF page 14, column 3) calls FIGS. 1A–1B a resistive element according to one embodiment of the invention; FIG. 2 a resistive element according to certain embodiments; FIG. 3A an array of patterned resistive elements; and FIGS. 3B and 3C 200 mm wafer four-point probe measurement locations and resistance values. en.summary: Claim 1 is a method of making an article. The method comprises providing a substrate; applying carbon nanotube growth catalyst on to a surface of the substrate; subjecting the substrate to a chemical vapor deposition of a carbon-containing gas to grow a non-woven fabric of carbon nanotubes, wherein the nanotubes of the fabric are substantially parallel to said surface of the substrate; selectively removing portions of the non-woven fabric according to a defined pattern; and providing first and second electrodes in contact with respective first and second portions of the patterned non-woven fabric to create the article, wherein the patterned non-woven fabric forms a conductive trace between the first and second electrodes. “On to” is printed as two words and is recorded as printed. Claim 1 of this grant was transcribed from this official PDF and was not copied from related US7335395B2. This is a bounded textual technical review, not a legal determination of claim scope.
limitations: The claimed object is a method of making an article.

The substrate is subjected to a chemical vapor deposition of a carbon-containing gas to grow a non-woven fabric of carbon nanotubes, the nanotubes of the fabric being substantially parallel to said surface of the substrate.
Portions of the non-woven fabric are selectively removed according to a defined pattern.

First and second electrodes are provided in contact with respective first and second portions of the patterned non-woven fabric to create the article, and the patterned non-woven fabric forms a conductive trace between those electrodes.

Claims 18–24 limit the carbon-containing gas to methane or ethylene and recites specific temperatures, flow rates, and inert gasses (argon, hydrogen, and a 1:4 ratio). Claim 25 further includes oxidizing the substrate before chemical vapor deposition. Claim 26 limits the growth catalysts to nanoparticles having specific diameters. Claims 27–29 concern controlling or selectively removing metallic and semiconducting nanotubes. Those catalyst forms, gas and process parameters, and metallic/semiconducting selection are not folded into Claim 1.

(a) a nanotube element comprising a nanotube fabric, the nanotube element having a top surface, a bottom surface, and a plurality of side surfaces;

en.summary: Claim 1 is a covered nanotube switch. The switch comprises: (a) a nanotube element comprising a nanotube fabric, the nanotube element having a top surface, a bottom surface, and a plurality of side surfaces; (b) first and second conductive terminals in contact with the nanotube element, wherein the first conductive terminal is disposed on and substantially covering the entire top surface of the nanotube element, and wherein the second conductive terminal contacts at least a portion of the bottom surface of the nanotube element; and (c) control circuitry in electrical communication with and capable of applying electrical stimulus to the first and second conductive terminals, wherein the nanotube element is capable of switching between a plurality of electronic states in response to a corresponding plurality of electrical stimuli applied by the control circuitry to the first and second conductive terminals, and wherein, for each different electronic state of the plurality of electronic states, the nanotube element provides an electrical pathway of corresponding different resistance between the first and second conductive terminals. The printed phrasing “disposed on and substantially covering,” and the shift from singular “electrical stimulus” in (c) to plural “electrical stimuli” in the first wherein clause, are recorded as printed. This is a bounded textual technical review, not a legal determination of claim scope.
limitations: The claimed object is a covered nanotube switch.
A nanotube element comprising a nanotube fabric has a top surface, a bottom surface, and a plurality of side surfaces.

First and second conductive terminals are in contact with the nanotube element: the first is disposed on and substantially covering the entire top surface, and the second contacts at least a portion of the bottom surface.
Control circuitry is in electrical communication with, and capable of applying electrical stimulus to, the first and second conductive terminals.

The nanotube element is capable of switching between a plurality of electronic states in response to a corresponding plurality of electrical stimuli applied by the control circuitry to those terminals.
For each different electronic state, the nanotube element provides an electrical pathway of corresponding different resistance between the first and second conductive terminals.
en.dependentClaimBoundary: The independent claims are Claim 1, Claim 11 (page 72, column 44, continuing onto page 73, column 45), and Claim 19 (page 73, column 46). Claims 2–10 depend from 1; claims 12–18 depend from 11; and claims 20–21 depend from 19. The grant prints 21 claims, matching the front-page footer, and all 21 are device claims to a covered nanotube switch. Claims 2–3 further require the first terminal also to cover at least one, or the plurality, of the side surfaces. Claims 4–6 introduce an insulator layer and its materials (SiO₂, SiN, and Al₂O₃). Claims 7–8 introduce a passivation layer and its materials. Claim 9 further requires the second terminal to contact substantially the entire bottom surface. Claim 10 lists conductive-material options for the terminals. Claims 11 and 19 are a different structure, with the terminals in spaced relation to each other and first and second insulator layers that together substantially surround the nanotube element. That surrounding-insulator structure, and an “unaligned plurality of nanotubes,” are not folded into Claim 1.
en.specificationBoundary: The brief description of the drawings (PDF page 53, columns 5–6, headed “BRIEF DESCRIPTION OF THE DRAWINGS,” and opening “In the drawings:” as printed) calls FIGS. 1A–1C perspective drawings of two-terminal nonvolatile nanotube switch (NV NT switch) embodiments with bottom contact locations, combined top/side and bottom contact locations, and top and bottom contact locations. FIG. 2A is an NV NT switch in an essentially horizontal orientation with two bottom contact terminals on opposite ends of a patterned nanotube channel element; FIG. 2B is an SEM of a similar switch; and FIG. 2C shows cycling results for a similar switch. FIG. 3 is likewise a horizontally oriented NV NT switch with two bottom contact terminals on opposite ends of a patterned nanotube channel element, in which the switch channel length is less than the spacing between contact terminals. These figures illustrate nanotube-block and channel-switch embodiments. They cannot be used to rewrite Claim 1, and the two-bottom-contact layout, the channel-length-to-spacing relationship, insulator or passivation layers, memory arrays, and cycling data are not folded into Claim 1. The abstract’s “unaligned plurality of nanotubes” does not appear in the text of Claim 1 and is not folded in.

en.summary: Claim 1 is a non-volatile memory. The memory comprises a bit line, a word line, at least one non-volatile memory cell, each having a two-terminal nanotube switching device and a cell selection circuit, write control circuitry, resistance sensing circuitry, and read circuitry. The switching device comprises first and second conductive terminals and a nanotube fabric article disposed between and in electrical communication with those terminals. The cell selection circuit is in electrical communication with the bit line and the word line to select the switching device for read and write operations in response to activation of at least one of the bit line and the word line. The second multi-layer carbon block is in electrical communication with the first multi-layer carbon block.
The first and second multi-layer carbon blocks comprise a diode carbon layer.

en.summary: Claim 1 is a field effect device. The device comprises a source region and a drain region of a first semiconductor type and a channel region disposed therebetween of a second semiconductor type, the drain region being connected to a corresponding terminal. A gate structure is disposed over the channel region and connected to a corresponding terminal. A nanotube switching element, responsive to a first control terminal and a second control terminal, is electrically positioned in series between the source region and a terminal corresponding to the source region, and is electromechanically operable to one of an open and closed state to thereby open or close an electrical communication path between the source region and its corresponding terminal. When the nanotube switching element is in the closed state, the channel conductivity and operation of the device is responsive to electrical stimulus at the terminals corresponding to the source and drain regions and the gate structure. The printed wording “electromechanically” (unhyphenated), “one of an open and closed state,” and the singular “is responsive” are recorded as printed. This is a bounded textual technical review, not a legal determination of claim scope.
limitations: The claimed object is a field effect device.

A gate structure disposed over the channel region and connected to a corresponding terminal.

A nanotube switching element, responsive to a first control terminal and a second control terminal, electrically positioned in series between the source region and a terminal corresponding to the source region.

The nanotube switching element is electromechanically operable to one of an open and closed state to thereby open or close an electrical communication path between the source region and its corresponding terminal.

When the nanotube switching element is in the closed state, the channel conductivity and operation of the device is responsive to electrical stimulus at the terminals corresponding to the source and drain regions and the gate structure.

Claims 4–5, 7–10, and 13 depend directly from 1 and further limit a dielectric surface on the control terminal and a non-volatile open state, source/drain/gate and control-terminal voltage levels, inversion of channel conductivity type, a substantially monolayer fabric of nanotubes, reference and release electrodes forming a non-volatile open state, and signal routing in closed and open states. Claims 11–12 depend from 9 and further recites a set electrode forming a non-volatile closed state. Claim 8 depends from Claim 1 yet refers to “the fabric,” a term first introduced in claim 2. note.zh: FIGS. 1(A)、1(B) 與 1(C) 在第 12 頁（Sheet 1 of 20），為製程剖面，標號含基板／氧化層 100、102、104，凹穴 106，支撐 110，以及電極 112。FIGS. 1(D)–1(F) 在第 13 頁，1(G)–1(I) 在第 14 頁，1(J)–1(L) 在第 15 頁，1(M)–1(O) 在第 16 頁，1(P) 在第 17 頁；帶撇的 1(I') 與 1(J') 在第 18 頁，1(K') 在第 19 頁。附圖簡述（第 33 頁第 3 欄）稱 FIGS. 1A-P 與 1I'-1K' 為形成水平配置奈米管物件過程中之中間結構剖面。這些製程中間步驟不是 Claim 1 的物件限制，不能用來改寫 Claim 1。
note.en: FIGS. 1(A), 1(B), and 1(C) are on PDF page 12 (Sheet 1 of 20). They are process cross-sections, with references including substrate/oxide layers 100, 102, and 104, cavity 106, supports 110, and electrode 112. FIGS. 1(D)–1(F) are on page 13, 1(G)–1(I) on page 14, 1(J)–1(L) on page 15, 1(M)–1(O) on page 16, and 1(P) on page 17; primed views 1(I') and 1(J') are on page 18 and 1(K') on page 19. The brief description (page 33, column 3) calls FIGS. 1A-P and 1I'-1K' cross-sectional diagrams of intermediate structures created during process of forming a device having a horizontally disposed nanotube article. Those in-process intermediate steps are not limitations of Claim 1’s article and cannot be used to rewrite Claim 1.

note.zh: FIGS. 2(A)–2(C) 在第 20 頁（Sheet 9 of 20），為結構 182、183、188 的剖面，標號含 112、116、154、168、178、180、185、186。FIG. 2(D) 在第 21 頁（Sheet 10），為結構 192，顯示偏轉的奈米織物 154 與標號 194、196、168、112；該圖也出現在首頁摘要圖。附圖簡述稱 FIGS. 2A-D 說明可在製造中控制懸空奈米管物件與電極間隙、並說明金屬化方案的實施例。那些間隙控制與金屬化細節不能折入 Claim 1。
note.en: FIGS. 2(A)–2(C) are on PDF page 20 (Sheet 9 of 20). They are cross-sections of structures 182, 183, and 188, with references including 112, 116, 154, 168, 178, 180, 185, and 186. FIG. 2(D) is on page 21 (Sheet 10) and is structure 192, showing deflected nanofabric 154 and references 194, 196, 168, and 112; that view also appears as the front-page abstract figure. The brief description says FIGS. 2A-D illustrate embodiments in which the gap displacement between a suspended nanotube article and an electrode may be controlled during fabrication, and also a metallization scheme. Those gap-control and metallization details are not folded into Claim 1.

note.zh: FIG. 3 在第 22 頁（Sheet 11 of 20），圖名印載為 “Figure 3”。該圖是中間結構 176 的平面圖，帶有剖面線 A–A'、B–B'、C–C'，標號含 102、116、154、165、168。附圖簡述稱 FIG. 3 為依實施例的中間結構平面圖。這些剖面線與特定標號不能折入 Claim 1。
note.en: FIG. 3 is on PDF page 22 (Sheet 11 of 20), labeled “Figure 3.” It is a plan view of intermediate structure 176, with section lines A–A', B–B', and C–C' and references 102, 116, 154, 165, and 168. The brief description calls FIG. 3 a plan view of an intermediate structure according to certain embodiments of the invention. Those section lines and particular reference numbers are not folded into Claim 1.
